title: Orbit
text:
Orbit

Alternative to HubSpot

Also replaces Pipedrive, Salesforce

A CRM that shows which deal to work next, and why.

Orbit in 51 seconds
The NOW queue of deals to act on
Your brief: what changed since last look
Review a follow-up before it is sent
Signal sources feeding the queue

run-orbit.com
↗
GitHub
→

Orbit puts a deal in your NOW queue when a customer replies, scores it from real signals, and shows you why. Your company's policy controls agent sending; with approval required, a person reviews the exact email before it is sent. It is free for the whole team, and you can try it beside your current CRM.

What it does
Move a deal into your NOW queue when a customer replies, books a meeting or submits a form
Score each deal from what customers actually did, with older activity counting for less and every signal behind the score shown
Keep contacts, companies and deals, with your own fields, in a pipeline with your own stages
Let a contact form on your site drop each enquiry onto the right contact
Draft follow-ups, with optional AI, that you review and approve one by one, and schedule them with quiet hours
Cancel scheduled follow-ups automatically when the customer replies
Pull in emails and meetings from Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, forwarded mail or a calendar link
Import contacts from a CSV, and export or restore a complete archive of your workspace any time
What it promises
Signals, scores and AI text never grant permission to send. Your company's policy decides agent sending; when approval is required, a person approves the exact saved recipients, subject and body, and later changes invalidate it.
A deal's score shows every signal it used, with source, time and weight, beside the reason for the recommendation.
Orbit uses no tracking script, pixel or cookie, and does not fingerprint visitors.
A reply, a booked meeting, an unsubscribe or a permanent bounce cancels that contact's scheduled messages.
Opt-out is on by default for sequence email and off for one-to-one email. Messages set to carry it include one-click unsubscribe; an identified opt-out marks the contact do-not-contact within a minute and cancels scheduled messages.
A draft goes stale when the customer replies or the deal changes, and a stale draft cannot be sent until you have seen what changed.
Capture never writes a draft or sends a message, and a contact created from captured mail is do-not-contact until you clear it.
If the AI is unavailable, records, scoring, search, hand-written drafts and sending still work.
Merging duplicates needs you to choose the surviving record and every conflicting value, and refuses if either record changed after your review.
Deleting a contact removes their email, signals, drafts and message bodies from records, search, exports and later AI or mail requests within five minutes.

title: Spool
text:
Spool

Alternative to Sentry

Also replaces Bugsnag, Rollbar

JavaScript errors, traced to the exact line in your source.

Spool in 51 seconds
New errors, grouped into issues
One issue, mapped to your original source
Filter issues by release, status and project

run-spool.com
↗
GitHub
→

Spool catches the errors in your app, groups repeats into one issue and points to the exact line in your own source code where it broke. It tells you when a fixed error comes back in a later release, and gives your coding agent a read-only view of one project's evidence.

What it does
Catch errors from JavaScript, Python and Go apps, using the same reporting libraries Sentry uses
Group repeats into a single issue and show exactly where in your original source each error happened
Keep your source maps private and match them to the right release
Download an evidence packet to hand to whoever is fixing the issue
Create a read-only agent key so a coding agent can read one project's issues and evidence, and change nothing
Reopen a resolved issue when it returns in a later release, and name that release
Scrub emails, tokens and passwords before anything is saved
Export everything to one file and restore it into a fresh copy
What it promises
Error details are scrubbed before they are stored: emails, tokens and passwords are removed, and headers, cookies and request bodies are not kept by default.
Owner sign-in, error sending and read-only agent access are separate, revoking one takes effect on the next request, and your source maps are never public.
An error is only counted once it is fully saved, and a repeated send never counts twice.
Changes to an issue are recorded, and a resolved issue reopens as returning only when it appears in a later release, so an old release's error raises no false alarm.
The evidence packet is size-limited and never includes your source code.
Counts of errors accepted and rejected are visible, and a quiet period is never reported as proof an error is fixed.

title: HappyToHelp
text:
HappyToHelp

Alternative to Zendesk

Also replaces Intercom, Help Scout, Freshdesk

Your Codex or Claude fixes the problem and writes the reply.

HappyToHelp in 56 seconds
A support conversation beside the AI helper
Move in your support history from an export

happytohelp.com
↗
GitHub
→

HappyToHelp is a customer support desk where your own Codex or Claude investigates the problem, fixes it and drafts the reply, and you press Send. It brings a website chat widget, a shared inbox for chat and email, a help center and replies drafted from your own articles into one place. You can try it beside your current helpdesk and bring your history over when you are ready.

What it does
Let your own Codex or Claude, running on your computer, investigate a customer's problem, fix it and draft the reply for you to send
Put a chat widget on your website that offers a hand when a visitor seems stuck
Answer chat and email from one shared inbox, with customer details beside each conversation, assignment rules, saved-reply macros, snoozing and merging of duplicates
Publish a searchable help center that customers use to find answers themselves
Get suggested replies drafted from your own articles, with the source shown
Collect a thumbs up or down on resolved conversations and see reports you can export
Connect with scoped API tokens, signed webhooks and Slack
Bring over your help center and history from Zendesk, Help Scout, Intercom or Freshdesk while your current helpdesk keeps running
What it promises
Imports are reviewed before anything is written, send no messages to your customers, can be undone as a whole, and keep source dates, private notes and publication state.
Customer and agent messages are stored once, and two conflicting final replies can never both be accepted.
Customers can rate a resolution with a thumbs up or down and a short comment, and comments are removed if the contact is erased.
Reports use your own calendar and time zone, count each conversation once, and export to a spreadsheet file that is safe to open.
Messages are saved before they are shown live, so a reload or dropped connection recovers everything that was sent, and an AI draft never becomes a final answer until it is safely accepted.
With no AI key, the AI is simply not assigned to new conversations and your team keeps them; your company's policy sets AI spending limits and uncertain attempts are never silently repeated.
Revoking a computer's access ends its authority at once, and HappyToHelp never claims that work already running there was stopped.
API tokens have chosen scopes, are shown once, are stored hashed and can expire; an unclear webhook result is not sent again.
Teammates can sign in with an authenticator app or a security key plus one-time recovery codes, and an owner can require it for everyone or by role.
You can export your conversations, files, contacts, help articles, settings and history in one checked archive and restore it into a clean installation; sign-ins and provider secrets are left out.

→

title: Oncall
text:
Oncall

Alternative to PagerDuty

Also replaces Opsgenie

Who's on now, who's next, and when they hand over.

Oncall in 54 seconds
A live incident with runbook and decision log
Who is on call, and the coverage windows
Incident timeline with follow-up owners

run-oncall.com
↗
GitHub
→

Oncall shows everyone who is on call now, who is next and exactly when they hand over. It keeps rotations, swaps, incidents, runbooks and follow-ups in one place, and runs alongside the pager you already use while you move your schedules over.

What it does
Show who is on call now, who is next and when the next hand-over happens
Build primary and backup rotations in your team's timezone, so a hand-over stays on the same clock time when clocks change
Cover a few hours with an override or swap without touching the rotation
Subscribe to a private calendar feed of the next seven days of shifts
Record alerts from monitoring, route them to the right service and replay the routing safely
Declare an incident, assign a commander, follow the runbook and keep every decision on a timeline
Resolve with recovery evidence and a summary, then track follow-up tasks and review
Preview your Opsgenie or PagerDuty schedules before anything is imported
What it promises
Oncall sends no texts, calls or push alerts, so your existing pager stays in charge while you use it.
Oncall sends signed response events only to endpoints an administrator approves; paging stays off, and email is for sign-in links only.
A runbook is copied into the incident when it is declared, so later edits never rewrite instructions mid-incident.
Resolving an incident needs recovery evidence and a summary, and every change is recorded in an attributed timeline.
Incident records you write are never deleted automatically.
Rotations hand over by wall-clock time in your named zone, and clock-change gaps show up as visible gaps.
Viewers can only read, responders coordinate, and admins manage; alert-sending credentials grant no read access, and removed access stops on the next request.
Replaying alert routing only reads: it creates no alert, incident or outside effect.
A move-in preview writes nothing, a person must review it before it is applied, and imported schedules stay paused.
A move-in can be undone, and edits you made afterwards are kept rather than overwritten.

→
